A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TGA study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching the retained case studies across their relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original safety evaluations, layer-intervention experiments, TGA benchmark results, and retrieval ablations in Sections 3–5.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds robustness experiments and comparison results in Appendix A.2, Tables 4–9.

M1.justification: Section 5 retains the same TGA architecture, BEIT-3 retrieval, caption guidance, hidden-state alignment, and training losses. Algorithm 1 is also unchanged. The additional filter and safety-aligned models are experimental comparators.

E1.justification: Appendix A.2 extends evaluation beyond the original toxic-image categories to SIUO's individually safe but jointly unsafe image–text inputs, plus role-play, in-context learning, and FigStep jailbreak scenarios. The original safety datasets and general-vision benchmarks remain.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated comparisons with the Tovilag defense and ECSO in Table 7, a trained ViT image filter in Table 8, and an LVLM constructed from a safety-aligned LLM in Table 9. Tovilag previously supplied evaluation data but was not evaluated as a defense comparator. Original comparator sets remain.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce a 100k training subset with caption replacement/deletion at 0–20% corruption, SIUO Safe Rate evaluation, jailbreak testing, and filter/backbone controls. The filter uses mixed toxic and normal training images. These substantially extend the evaluation design; the original main-experiment settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds caption-error sensitivity, unsafe-composition robustness, and three jailbreak tests in Tables 4–6, alongside filter and safety-aligned-backbone controls in Tables 8–9. Existing layer interventions, retrieval ablations, and all seven case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Table 1 retains the same t-test significance markings and p-value threshold of 0.05. v2 introduces no additional run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or uncertainty-estimation procedures; its new tables report single values.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 retain their values, while Tables 4–9 add substantial results. For example, the new caption-noise study reports DSR declining from 18.57 at 0% corruption to 17.03 at 20%; SIUO Safe Rate is 30.77 for TGA versus 21.56 and 22.16 for LLaVA-v1.5-7B and 13B. These are additional evaluations, not revised original scores.

T1.justification: Equations 1–8 and the mathematical definitions underlying activation localization, attention analysis, hidden-state reconstruction, and TGA losses remain unchanged. The new filter 'upper bound' is an empirical comparison, without a mathematical derivation or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: explaining failed safety transfer through hidden-state misalignment and proposing TGA to transfer textual safety without visual safety fine-tuning while maintaining general capabilities. The appendix additions support these retained claims.

C2.justification: Appendix A.2 adds interpretations concerning caption dependence and compositional robustness. New Appendix A.4 identifies failures involving overlooked harmful objects, bloody images, and images that are difficult to caption correctly. These provide targeted qualifications while retaining the central mechanism explanation.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-availability statement and repository URL, plus setup details for the new caption-corruption and filter experiments. Existing architecture, GPU resources, learning rates, training epochs, and retrieval implementation details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds ECSO/Gou et al. and three retrieval-augmented-generation references, with a brief appendix comparison against detoxification and post-hoc defenses. The main related-work framing remains. The added Bianchi preprint entry corresponds to the already cited Safety-Tuned LLaMAs work.

P1.justification: The main narrative receives limited grammar and terminology edits, updated affiliations, acknowledgments, and a content warning. Appendix A.2 becomes additional experiments, the existing case-study section moves to A.3, and A.4 adds failure discussion. The corrected Section 3 sample-total typo does not establish changed data.

P2.justification: New Tables 4–9 substantially expand the visual presentation with dedicated sensitivity, compositional-safety, jailbreak, and defense-control comparisons. Original Tables 1–3 and Figures 2–14 are retained; Figure 1 receives small graphical adjustments, and the case-study figures move later in the appendix.

improvement.justification: The new appendix tests address previously untested caption dependence and adversarial/compositional inputs, while explicit failure conditions and a code link improve transparency. The gain is limited by terse experimental specifications and Table 8's unexplained repetition of all Table 6 role-play scores, which leaves the upper-bound comparison's setting unclear.
